clue.text: An enterprise with grave consequences

definitions.meaning: a venture or project someone takes on
read whimsically as the business of an undertaker, whose work ends at the graveside

explanation.surface: A risky business venture that ends with serious fallout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like 'serious', but it means a burial plot: the trade of a funeral director.
explanation.definitionFit: A project or venture taken on is a synonym; the funeral director's trade supplies the second, punning sense.

clue.text: Still wild about nude, tam?

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about someone wearing only a Scottish bonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NUDE and TAM together. A tam is a tam-o'-shanter, a Scottish woollen cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never domesticated and still wild has not been broken in by people.

clue.text: Disreputable bar right in a private road

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for right goes inside the word for the bar

parts.note: a dive is a seedy, disreputable bar

explanation.surface: A seedy pub has somehow been put on someone's private road.
explanation.walkthrough: A drive is the private road leading up to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The short private track from street to house is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Greek in trouble for smoking

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things messed up, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Greek person in difficulties because they were caught smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal for the letters of GREEK IN; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a container word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something giving off fumes or smoke is literally emitting vapour, the older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Herod is not to finish the Italian food

indicators.note: says the closing letters 'to' are not included at the finish of the food word

parts.note: antipasto is the Italian starter course of cold meats and vegetables

explanation.surface: A ruler declines to clear his plate of Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: Herod Antipas was the ruler of Galilee in the Gospels; drop the final TO from ANTIPASTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, is the Herod of the New Testament crucifixion story.

clue.text: When civil servants keep changing train time, they're annoying

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so the servants' letters surround the rest

parts.note: IRS, the Internal Revenue Service, is the US tax-collecting arm of the civil service

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters of train are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats who keep altering the train timetable are a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' puts RITAN (the anagram of TRAIN, from 'changing') plus T inside IRS, splitting it as IR...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that irritate or provoke are, by definition, annoying ones.

clue.text: Those who complain of tummy-ache and hollow rumbles

definitions.text: Those who complain of tummy-ache and hollow rumbles

parts.words: Those who complain of tummy-ache and hollow rumbles
parts.note: people who moan are said to gripe, and gripes are also stomach cramps, so moaners and colic merge

explanation.surface: People grumbling about stomach pains and an empty, rumbling belly.
explanation.walkthrough: Gripe means both to grumble and a sharp pain in the bowels, so the whole clue plays on both.
explanation.definitionFit: Complainers or grumblers, with a nod to stomach cramps called the gripes.

clue.text: Survive as a hobo?

definitions.meaning: to last longer than someone else
a tramp lives out of doors, sleeping rough

explanation.surface: Wondering whether getting by is like being a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as OUT LIVE: to live outdoors. Hobo is American for a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain alive after another has died is to last beyond them, a synonym of survive.

clue.text: Able to see but turning a blind eye

definitions.meaning: a window or house with a view over the landscape
ignoring or failing to notice a fault deliberately

explanation.surface: Someone who has sight yet chooses to ignore things.
explanation.definitionFit: A building commanding a view looks out over land, and to ignore something is to fail to notice it.

clue.text: A soldier could retire, right?

indicators.note: could here stands for could become, so the letters of retire are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a serviceman might now go into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could' is the anagram signal on RETIRE. In Britain a terrier is slang for a member of the Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A Territorial Army reservist is nicknamed this, from the first syllables of Territorial.

clue.text: Spits, cooking food!

parts.note: spits are not spitting but rotating skewers on which meat is roasted

explanation.surface: Someone spitting while preparing a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spits' looks like a verb about saliva; it is the plural noun for roasting skewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotating roasting spits used to cook meat over heat.

clue.text: She gives two points to me for English

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are two compass points

explanation.surface: A woman awards a pair of points to the speaker for an English essay.
explanation.walkthrough: Esmée is a woman's name, so 'She' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, so any woman bearing it may be called she.

clue.text: I am under the doctor and fed-up with waiting!

parts.note: contracted to I'm
someone under a doctor's care is a patient

explanation.surface: A hospital patient grumbles about the long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the doctor' is a British idiom for being treated by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and annoyed at delay is the plain sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Settling in temporary accommodation

definitions.meaning: coming to rest or becoming lodged in a place

explanation.surface: Getting comfortable in a short-term let.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented room is a place to stay, and something becoming stuck in place is settling there.

clue.text: I am inclined to be fair

parts.note: contracted to I'm
partial to something means inclined towards it

explanation.surface: Someone claims a tendency to be just.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is ironic: being partial is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unbiased and even-handed is being just and equitable.

clue.text: Cavities centrally placed, sometimes in use simultaneously

indicators.note: says the answer sits in the middle of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Hollows positioned in the middle are sometimes all in use at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is spread across 'sometimeS IN USE Simultaneously'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow air-filled spaces in the skull bones are a kind of cavity.

clue.text: A month to work on American swimmer

parts.note: Oct. is the abbreviation for October
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Spending a month on a job for a US swimming champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person; it is a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed sea creature that moves through the water is a swimmer.

clue.text: Senior pole reported aboard ship

parts.note: the highest mast section on a sailing vessel, senior as in uppermost

explanation.surface: An elderly Polish man has been reported as being on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland but means a spar; 'senior' means top.
explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost section of a ship's spar, above the lower spar, is the highest pole on board.

clue.text: A drunk in the passageway, needing something to eat

indicators.note: in places the passage word inside the word for the drunk

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
a hall is an entrance passage

explanation.surface: A drunk lying in the corridor needs food.
explanation.walkthrough: HALL goes inside SOT, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A small onion-like bulb is a vegetable eaten in cooking.

clue.text: An upper-class fool at first, whom maturity will soften

parts.note: an ass is a fool
U is the British label for upper-class usage
age means maturity

explanation.surface: A posh idiot who will mellow in later years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' places ASS U (an upper-class fool) before AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or relieve pain or anger is to soothe or mitigate it.

clue.text: Love goddess with a heavenly body and two front teeth

parts.note: a star is a heavenly body

indicators.note: the two front letters of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: A goddess of love with a celestial figure and prominent front teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two front' takes TE from 'teeth'. Astarte was the Phoenician goddess of love and fertility.
explanation.definitionFit: Astarte was the Phoenician deity of love and fertility, akin to Aphrodite.

clue.text: Let mail be collected up to now

indicators.note: letters gathered together in a new arrangement, so the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Instructions to let the post be picked up so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' suggests a postal pickup; it shuffles LET MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that is all-time is the best ever, up to the present moment.

clue.text: It's significant that I am left with worker

parts.note: contracted to I'm
port is the left side of a ship
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone claims importance though left alone with a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of consequence and weight is meaningful or notable.

clue.text: Indian food could get cold at sea

indicators.note: says the curry could gain the letter for cold and so become a sea's name

parts.note: the Baltic is the sea of northern Europe

explanation.surface: A curry might go cold when served on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: add C (cold) to the curry and you get BALTIC, a sea. 'at sea' looks like confusion but names it.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal pan, popular in Birmingham.

clue.text: Backfiring missile hitting a black deer

indicators.note: backfiring sends things back the way they came, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: IBM, an intercontinental ballistic missile
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A missile misfires and hits a black deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backfiring' turns the whole run IBM A B around; 'hitting' just joins the missile to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the fawn of Disney's film, so a young deer.

clue.text: From Ghana there's a song to lake crocodile

parts.note: GH is the international code for Ghana
an aria is a solo song in opera
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A crocodile from West Africa is serenaded beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The gharial is a long-snouted Indian crocodilian.
explanation.definitionFit: The gharial is a fish-eating reptile of the crocodile family from India.

clue.text: Stays on to fetch what's left

definitions.meaning: keeps staying or is left over

explanation.surface: Someone stays behind to collect the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay behind is the verb sense; the leftovers or ruins are the noun sense.

clue.text: Watch watch

parts.note: the first word is the timepiece, the second is a verb describing what the timepiece does by showing the hour

explanation.surface: A command to observe a wristwatch.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word switches part of speech: a watch is a timepiece, and to do this is what it does.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or wristwatch exists to show the hour, reading hours and minutes from its face.
